content.summary: Aga Khan University Hospital has added the most modern treatment for haemorrhoids called the Procedure for Prolapse and Haemorrhoids (PPH) to its existing facilities.

media.alt: Modern treatment for Haemorrhoids now available at AKUH: Half the population above the age of 30 suffers from haemorrhoids

content.text: Aga Khan University Hospital has added the most modern treatment for haemorrhoids called the Procedure for Prolapse and Haemorrhoids (PPH) to its existing facilities. In this regard, visiting Indian expert Dr Roysuneel V Patankar delivered a presentation on the latest method of haemorrhoidectomy at a seminar on piles arranged by Aga Khan University on June 1.
Dr Patankar is Associate Professor and Consultant at the Institute of Special Surgery in Mumbai and is on a five- day visit to Pakistan to conduct training for the new surgical treatment.
In his presentation, he discussed the benefits of the new method to patients, hospitals, surgeons and employers as well as the challenges and future of the PPH.

Assistant Professor and Consultant, Section of General Surgery, Department of Surgery at AKU Dr Tabish Chawla recounted the experience of PPH at AKU and pointed out that according to rough estimates, more than half the population above the age of 30 is likely to suffer from haemorrhoids which becomes a large figure in Karachi only. He said, "For years, physicians and patients have been awaiting a surgical treatment for haemorrhoids that causes less pain and a shorter recovery period than the traditional procedures. Now, we have one."

A panel discussion followed which included Dr Khalid Hameed, Associate Professor and Head, Section of General Surgery and Dr Rizwan Azami, Associate Professor and Consultant, Section of General Surgery, Department of Surgery.

Interim Study results from on going clinical trials in US show that patients who had undergone PPH suffered less over all adverse events and significantly less pain than reported in the traditional method. Using a special stapling device, the PPH Procedure essentially repositions the tissue and reduces blood flow to internal haemorrhoids. This method affects fewer nerve endings than the traditional one.

As a part of its social responsibility and commitment to the advancement of health research and education, AKU regularly holds seminars, symposiums and events to raise awareness about health and education related issues which are of national importance and interest. AKUH ensures the consistency of its high quality care through a meticulous process of continual quality assurance and constant upgrading of its services and equipment.
